Business insurance

Marine Cargo Insurance in Kenya

Marine cargo insurance protects goods against loss or damage while they move by sea, air or combined transport. For importers and exporters, it also produces the insurance certificate that banks, buyers and authorities may ask for.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Loss or damage to cargo in transit, on the terms selected
  • Cover for single shipments or ongoing movements under an open policy
  • Cover by sea, air, road or combined transit, depending on the policy
  • Insurance certificates for shipping documents

Who needs it

  • Importers bringing in stock, machinery or materials
  • Exporters of produce and manufactured goods
  • Clearing and forwarding firms advising clients
  • Businesses shipping on CIF, FOB or other trade terms

Common risks

Valuation gaps

Cargo is normally insured for invoice value plus freight and a margin. A low declared value limits a claim.

Packing and handling

Inadequate packing can lead to exclusions. Document how goods were packed.

Trade terms confusion

Who is responsible for insurance depends on the trade terms in your contract.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Cover options vary, from named-perils to broad all-risks terms. Compare the clauses, not just the label.
  • Delay, inherent vice and insufficient packing are commonly excluded.
  • Regulatory requirements about marine insurance for imports can change. Confirm current rules before shipping.

What affects the premium

  • Type of goods
  • Value and volume
  • Route and mode of transport
  • Packing
  • Cover terms selected
  • Frequency of shipments

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Description and value of goods
  • Origin, destination and route
  • Mode of transport and shipping terms
  • Packing details
  • Shipment frequency

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Single shipment cover or an open policy?

A single shipment policy suits occasional movements. If you ship regularly, an open policy with declarations can be more practical. We help you compare.

Can I get the certificate quickly?

Timing depends on information provided and the insurer’s process. Having your shipping documents ready helps.
